name: Engineering
pullQuote: Engineering is mostly the discipline of finding out what will fail first.
overview: The engineering business works on automotive and industrial systems — the assemblies and sub-assemblies that sit inside somebody else's product or plant. It is work rarely seen by the end user and judged almost entirely on whether it holds up under conditions nobody described precisely in advance.

Because the output is a component rather than a finished thing, the relationship with the customer is technical before it is commercial. Most of the value is created in the conversation before anything is made, when a requirement is still loose enough to be improved.

approach.heading: Tolerances and consequences
body: A specification describes what should happen. The useful question is what happens at the edges of it — the tolerance stack that is individually acceptable and collectively not, the duty cycle nobody wrote down, the maintenance that will not actually be performed. Engineering here starts from those edges and works inward.

The group prefers to be involved early enough to change a design rather than late enough only to build it. A problem caught on a drawing costs a conversation; the same problem caught on a production line costs considerably more.
